overall: The AG found the Hamilton Board of Selectmen violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating without notice at a joint meeting of two other bodies; it declined the false-statement and parking-lot allegations and ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: A quorum of the Board allegedly deliberated at a joint meeting of two other bodies (Finance Committee and Affordable Housing Trust) for which the Board posted no notice.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating without posting notice during the September 5 meeting of the Hamilton Finance Committee and the Affordable Housing Trust.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a Board member made a false statement at the September 5 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Our office, however, does not review statements made during meetings to ensure they are factually true.

allegations.summary: The request for further review alleged a quorum improperly met in the parking lot after the meeting, a claim not raised in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review this allegation as it was not included in the original complaint to the Board and the Board has not had an opportunity to respond to it.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar violations in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
